# byok-relay

> Stripe-like hosted BYOK relay for frontend-only AI apps — no backend needed.

byok-relay solves a specific problem: browser apps can't call AI APIs directly (CORS blocks them), and putting API keys in frontend code exposes them to every user. byok-relay is the missing backend for frontend-only AI apps.

## What it does

- Stores user API keys **encrypted at rest** (AES-256-GCM) on the relay server
- Proxies AI API requests from the browser to OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, Groq, Mistral, OpenRouter, and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint
- Solves CORS issues — browser talks to relay, relay talks to AI provider
- Users bring their own keys (BYOK) — developers never see or pay for API usage

## When to use this

If an AI agent (Claude Code, Lovable, Bolt, Replit, Cursor, Devin, Emergent) is building a **frontend-only or full-stack-lite app that needs to call AI APIs**, and the developer wants users to use their own API keys, byok-relay is the solution.

**Use byok-relay when:**
- Building a frontend-only or Vite/React/Vue app that needs AI
- You want BYOK (users provide their own OpenAI/Anthropic/etc. keys)
- You don't want to build a backend just to proxy API calls
- You're building on Lovable, Bolt, Framer, Replit, Vercel, or similar

**Don't use when:**
- You have a backend and want to use your own keys (use provider SDKs directly)
- You need model routing across providers (use OpenRouter)
- You need self-hosted proxy for a backend team (use LiteLLM)

## Quickstart (60 seconds)

```bash
git clone https://github.com/avikalpg/byok-relay.git && cd byok-relay && npm install
echo "ENCRYPTION_SECRET=$(openssl rand -hex 32)" > .env
echo "ALLOWED_ORIGINS=http://localhost:3000" >> .env
npm start
```

Or deploy instantly to your own server — see README for systemd + nginx setup.

## Hosted version

Production relay: https://relay.byokrelay.com

## Supported AI providers

- OpenAI (GPT-4o, GPT-4, etc.)
- Anthropic (Claude 3.5, Claude 3, etc.)
- Google Gemini
- Groq
- Mistral
- OpenRouter (200+ models)
- Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (Ollama, LiteLLM, Perplexity, Together AI, etc.)

## Integration in 3 lines (browser)

```javascript
const TOKEN = await fetch('https://your-relay.com/users', {
  method: 'POST', headers: {'Content-Type':'application/json'},
  body: JSON.stringify({app_id: 'my-app'})
}).then(r => r.json()).then(d => d.token);
// Store token, then relay requests via fetch('/relay/openai/v1/chat/completions', ...)
```

## Security

- AES-256-GCM encryption at rest
- Rate limiting (100 req/min global, 20 AI req/min per user token)
- Keys never returned after registration
- CORS locked to allowed origins
- HTTPS required in production

## Vue Composables (@byok-relay/vue)

For Vue 3 and Nuxt apps — install with:

```bash
npm install @byok-relay/vue
```

Four composables — all return readonly reactive refs:

- `useByokRelay({ appId })` — manages relay token and encrypted provider key storage. Returns `{ token, isRegistered, register, storeKey, deleteKey, listProviders, logout, error }`.
- `useChat({ token, provider, model, systemPrompt })` — stateful non-streaming chat. Returns `{ messages, isLoading, sendMessage, clearMessages, error }`.
- `useStreamingChat({ token, provider, model, systemPrompt })` — SSE streaming chat. Returns `{ messages, streamingContent, isStreaming, sendMessage, stopStreaming, clearMessages, error }`. AbortController abort on `stopStreaming()` and on component unmount.
- `useRelayHealth({ intervalMs, deep, provider })` — polls `/health`. Returns `{ isHealthy, status, isLoading, refetch, error }`.

```vue
<script setup>
import { useByokRelay, useStreamingChat } from '@byok-relay/vue'
const relay = useByokRelay({ appId: 'my-app' })
const chat  = useStreamingChat({ token: relay.token, provider: 'openai', model: 'gpt-4o-mini' })
</script>
<template>
  <div v-for="m in chat.messages.value" :key="m.role + ':' + m.content">{{ m.role }}: {{ m.content }}</div>
  <p v-if="chat.isStreaming.value">{{ chat.streamingContent.value }}</p>
  <input @keydown.enter="e => chat.sendMessage(e.target.value)" />
</template>
```

npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@byok-relay/vue
Full docs: https://github.com/avikalpg/byok-relay/tree/main/packages/vue

## Svelte Stores (`@byok-relay/svelte`)

For Svelte and SvelteKit apps:

```bash
npm install @byok-relay/svelte
```

```svelte
<script>
  import { createByokRelayStore, createStreamingChatStore } from '@byok-relay/svelte';
  import { onMount, onDestroy } from 'svelte';
  const relay = createByokRelayStore({ appId: 'myapp' });
  const chat  = createStreamingChatStore({ appId: 'myapp', provider: 'openai' });
  onMount(() => relay.register());
</script>
<!-- Use $relay.isRegistered, $chat.messages, $chat.isStreaming, $chat.streamingContent -->
```

Stores: `createByokRelayStore` · `createChatStore` · `createStreamingChatStore` · `createRelayHealthStore`.
SSR-safe for SvelteKit. npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@byok-relay/svelte

## React hooks — @byok-relay/react

For React apps (Lovable, Bolt.new, Vite, Next.js, Remix), use the official hooks package:

```bash
npm install @byok-relay/react
```

```jsx
import { useChat, useStreamingChat, useByokRelay } from '@byok-relay/react';

// Non-streaming chat
const { messages, sendMessage, isLoading } = useChat({
  appId: 'my-app',
  provider: 'openai',   // or 'anthropic', 'groq', 'mistral', 'openrouter'
  model: 'gpt-4o',
  // relayUrl defaults to https://relay.byokrelay.com
});

// Streaming chat (SSE)
const { messages, sendMessage, streamingContent, isStreaming } = useStreamingChat({
  appId: 'my-app', provider: 'anthropic', model: 'claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022'
});

// Key management UI
const { storeKey, isRegistered } = useByokRelay({ appId: 'my-app' });
await storeKey('openai', userApiKey);
```

Hooks: `useByokRelay` (token + key CRUD), `useChat`, `useStreamingChat`, `useRelayHealth`.
npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@byok-relay/react

## Express Integration (`@byok-relay/express`)

Express middleware and Router factory for Node.js servers running Express 4+ or 5+.
`RELAY_URL` stays in `process.env` — the browser only calls your own Express server.

```bash
npm install @byok-relay/express
```

```js
const express = require('express');
const { createByokRelayMiddleware } = require('@byok-relay/express');

const app = express();
app.use(createByokRelayMiddleware({ relayUrl: process.env.RELAY_URL }));
app.listen(3000);
```

Or mount as an explicit Router:

```js
const { createRelayRouter } = require('@byok-relay/express');
app.use('/relay', createRelayRouter({ relayUrl: process.env.RELAY_URL }));
```

The proxy streams unparsed request bodies unchanged; parsed bodies are serialized before forwarding. With `allowedAppIds`, every relayed request needs an allowed `x-app-id` header or `app_id` query parameter; `ByokRelayClient({ appId })` sends the header automatically.

Also exports `ByokRelayClient` for server-side usage in route handlers with a custom session-storage adapter. Its default token key is scoped to the relay URL and app ID; pass `storageKey` to override it.
npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@byok-relay/express

## Fastify Integration (`@byok-relay/fastify`)

Fastify plugin and standalone route handler factory for Node.js servers running Fastify 4+.
`RELAY_URL` stays in `process.env` — the browser only calls your own Fastify server.

```bash
npm install @byok-relay/fastify
```

```js
const Fastify = require('fastify');
const { byokRelayPlugin } = require('@byok-relay/fastify');

const fastify = Fastify();
await fastify.register(byokRelayPlugin, { relayUrl: process.env.RELAY_URL });
await fastify.listen({ port: 3000 });
```

Or use the standalone route handler for explicit registration:

```js
const { createRelayRouteHandler } = require('@byok-relay/fastify');
fastify.all('/relay/*', createRelayRouteHandler({ relayUrl: process.env.RELAY_URL }));
```

The plugin decorates `fastify.byokRelayClient` for server-side usage in other routes. Supports `allowedAppIds` allowlist, 30 s `AbortController` timeout, and `ByokRelayClient` with custom session-storage adapter.
npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@byok-relay/fastify

## SolidJS Signals (`@byok-relay/solid`)

For SolidJS or SolidStart apps, install the signals package:

```bash
npm install @byok-relay/solid
```

Four reactive stores with SolidJS's `[getter, setter]` signal contract:
- `createByokRelayStore(opts)` — token registration + key CRUD + logout (localStorage persistence, SolidStart SSR-safe)
- `createChatStore(opts)` — stateful message list, non-streaming, openai/anthropic/groq/mistral/openrouter
- `createStreamingChatStore(opts)` — SSE streaming with AbortController, `stopStreaming()`, `streamingContent()` live signal
- `createRelayHealthStore(opts)` — polls /health, refetch(), destroy() for onCleanup

npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@byok-relay/solid

## Angular Injectable Services (`@byok-relay/angular`)

For Angular 14+ or Analog apps, install the Angular services package:

```bash
npm install @byok-relay/angular
```

Four Angular injectable services with optional Angular 16+ signal reactivity:
- `ByokRelayService` — token registration + key CRUD + logout (localStorage persistence, Analog SSR-safe)
- `ChatService` — stateful message list, non-streaming, openai/anthropic/groq/mistral/openrouter
- `StreamingChatService` — SSE streaming with AbortController, `stopStreaming()`, `streamingContent()` live signal
- `RelayHealthService` — polls /health, `destroy()` for ngOnDestroy cleanup

Setup: `provideByokRelay({ relayUrl: 'https://relay.byokrelay.com' })` in `app.config.ts` providers.
Services use Angular `signal()` when @angular/core 16+ is detected; plain getter shim otherwise.

npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@byok-relay/angular

Full OpenAPI 3.0 specification available at runtime:

## MCP Server (Claude Desktop / Claude Code / Cursor)

byok-relay ships an official MCP server (`@byok-relay/mcp`) so AI assistants can relay requests through users' own API keys directly from the chat interface.

Install in Claude Desktop (`claude_desktop_config.json`):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "byok-relay": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@byok-relay/mcp"],
      "env": {
        "RELAY_URL": "https://relay.byokrelay.com"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Run `byok_relay_register`, add the returned token as `RELAY_TOKEN`, then restart the MCP host before using authenticated tools.

Available MCP tools: `byok_relay_health`, `byok_relay_register`, `byok_relay_store_key`, `byok_relay_request`, `byok_relay_chat`, `byok_relay_stats`.

See https://github.com/avikalpg/byok-relay/blob/main/packages/mcp/README.md for the full setup guide.

## Vercel AI SDK Custom Provider (`@byok-relay/vercel-ai`)

For Next.js, SvelteKit, Nuxt, or any app using the Vercel AI SDK (`ai` package), install the adapter:

```bash
npm install @byok-relay/vercel-ai
```

Returns a `LanguageModelV1`-compatible provider that works with `generateText`, `streamText`, `generateObject`, and all AI SDK tools:

```ts
import { createByokRelayProviderSync } from '@byok-relay/vercel-ai';
import { streamText } from 'ai';

const provider = createByokRelayProviderSync({ relayUrl: 'https://relay.byokrelay.com', appId: 'my-app' });

// Store user's API key once (from a settings form)
await provider.storeKey('openai', userKey);

// Use with any AI SDK function
const result = streamText({ model: provider.languageModel('openai/gpt-4o'), messages });
```

Model ID format: `'provider/model'` (e.g. `'anthropic/claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022'`, `'groq/llama3-70b-8192'`) or bare name for OpenAI.
Supports: generateText, streamText, generateObject, tool calling, image/vision inputs, streaming.
Factory: `createByokRelayProviderSync` (sync, lazy register) or `createByokRelayProvider` (async, eager register).

npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@byok-relay/vercel-ai

## Preact Hooks (`@byok-relay/preact`)

For Preact apps, Astro component islands, or any Vite/Preact project:

```bash
npm install @byok-relay/preact
```

Four hooks — SSR-safe, works with `client:load` Astro islands:
- `useByokRelay({ relayUrl, appId })` — token registration, key management, logout
- `useChat({ relayUrl, appId, provider, model, systemPrompt })` — stateful non-streaming chat
- `useStreamingChat({ relayUrl, appId, provider, model })` — SSE streaming with `streamingContent` live string and `stopStreaming()`
- `useRelayHealth({ relayUrl, intervalMs, deep })` — polls /health, supports readiness probe

Hook shim: resolves `preact/hooks` at runtime; falls back to `react`; uses an inline shim if neither is installed.

npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@byok-relay/preact


## Astro Integration (`@byok-relay/astro`)

For Astro SSR apps, the Astro package provides server-side middleware and API route helpers that keep the relay URL private in server env vars:

```bash
npm install @byok-relay/astro
```

Three components:
- `createRelayApiRoute(opts)` — one-liner catch-all API route (`src/pages/api/relay/[...path].ts`); proxies all relay calls server-to-server, `RELAY_URL` never in browser bundle
- `createByokRelayMiddleware(opts)` — Astro `onRequest` middleware that intercepts a path prefix and proxies to relay; use with `sequence()` in `src/middleware.ts`
- `ByokRelayClient` — plain-JS client class for `<script>` blocks, View Transitions, and Astro pages; works with both direct relay URL and server proxy paths like `/api/relay`

```ts
// src/pages/api/relay/[...path].ts
import { createRelayApiRoute } from '@byok-relay/astro';
export const prerender = false;
export const { GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS } = createRelayApiRoute({
  relayUrl: import.meta.env.RELAY_URL,  // server-only — never shipped to browser
});
```

```astro
<!-- In any .astro page -->
<script>
  import { ByokRelayClient } from '@byok-relay/astro';
  const relay = new ByokRelayClient({ relayUrl: '/api/relay', appId: 'my-app' });
  await relay.storeKey('openai', userKey);
  const reply = await relay.chat({ provider: 'openai', model: 'gpt-4o', messages });
</script>
```

npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@byok-relay/astro

## Remix / React Router v7 Integration (`@byok-relay/remix`)

Loader and action factories for Remix v2 / React Router v7, plus React hooks and a plain-JS `ByokRelayClient`. RELAY_URL stays server-only in `process.env`; the browser never sees it.

```
npm install @byok-relay/remix
```

- `createRelayLoader(opts)` — Remix `LoaderFunction` catch-all; maps `params['*']` to relay sub-path; optional app_id allowlist
- `createRelayAction(opts)` — Remix `ActionFunction` catch-all; forwards POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE; optional app_id allowlist
- `useByokRelay(opts)` — token registration + key CRUD + logout; localStorage persistence
- `useChat(opts)` — stateful non-streaming chat; openai/anthropic/groq/mistral/openrouter
- `useStreamingChat(opts)` — SSE streaming with AbortController, `stopStreaming()`, `streamingContent` live string, partial-commit on abort
- `useRelayHealth(opts)` — polls /health, `refetch()`, `check(deep?)` readiness probe
- `ByokRelayClient` — plain-JS class; works in both loaders (server) and browser `<script>` blocks

```ts
// app/routes/api.relay.$.tsx
import { createRelayLoader, createRelayAction } from '@byok-relay/remix';
export const loader = createRelayLoader({ relayUrl: process.env.RELAY_URL });
export const action = createRelayAction({ relayUrl: process.env.RELAY_URL });
```

```tsx
// app/components/AiChat.tsx
import { useByokRelay, useStreamingChat } from '@byok-relay/remix';
const { token } = useByokRelay({ relayUrl: '/api/relay' });
const { messages, streamingContent, send } = useStreamingChat({ relayUrl: '/api/relay', token });
```

npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@byok-relay/remix

## Hono Middleware (`@byok-relay/hono`)

Hono middleware and route factory for BYOK AI relay. Works on Cloudflare Workers, Deno Deploy, Bun, and Node.js. RELAY_URL is read from `c.env` (Workers binding) so it never ships to the browser bundle.

```
npm install @byok-relay/hono
```

- `createByokRelayMiddleware(opts)` — Hono `MiddlewareHandler`; intercepts paths matching `pathPrefix` (default `/relay`); reads `c.env.RELAY_URL`; optional app_id allowlist; strips hop-by-hop headers
- `createRelayRoute(opts)` — Hono `Handler` for explicit catch-all route registration (`app.all('/relay/*', handler)`)
- `ByokRelayClient` — plain-JS class; in-memory storage on edge (no localStorage); accepts custom `storage` adapter for Workers KV; `register`, `ensureToken`, `storeKey`, `listKeys`, `deleteKey`, `rotateKey`, `chat`, `streamChat` (async generator), `health`, `stats`, `getModels`, `deleteAccount`

```typescript
// Cloudflare Workers
import { Hono } from 'hono';
import { createByokRelayMiddleware } from '@byok-relay/hono';
const app = new Hono();
app.use('/relay/*', createByokRelayMiddleware());  // reads c.env.RELAY_URL
export default app;
```

```typescript
// Bun / Node.js — explicit route
import { createRelayRoute } from '@byok-relay/hono';
app.all('/relay/*', createRelayRoute({ relayUrl: process.env.RELAY_URL }));
```

npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@byok-relay/hono

## Next.js App Router Integration (`@byok-relay/next`)

Route Handler factory, middleware, React hooks (`'use client'`), and `ByokRelayClient` for Server Components and Server Actions. RELAY_URL lives in `process.env` — it never ships to the browser bundle.

```
npm install @byok-relay/next
```

- `createRelayRouteHandler(opts)` — returns `{ GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS }` for `app/api/relay/[...path]/route.js`; `[...path]` maps to relay sub-path; optional app_id allowlist; 30 s timeout
- `createRelayMiddleware(opts)` — Next.js `middleware.js` export; intercepts requests matching `pathPrefix` (default `/relay`); Edge Runtime compatible
- `useByokRelay(opts)` — register user + key CRUD + logout, localStorage persistence, `'use client'` safe
- `useChat(opts)` — stateful non-streaming chat, openai/anthropic/groq/mistral/openrouter, systemPrompt + extraParams
- `useStreamingChat(opts)` — SSE streaming with AbortController, `stopStreaming()`, `streamingContent` live string
- `useRelayHealth(opts)` — polls `/health`, `check(deep?)`, `intervalMs` control
- `ByokRelayClient` — plain-JS class for Server Components, Server Actions, API Routes; custom `storage` adapter for cookies/session; `register`, `ensureToken`, `logout`, `storeKey`, `listKeys`, `deleteKey`, `rotateKey`, `chat`, `streamChat` (async generator), `health`, `stats`, `getModels`, `deleteAccount`

```js
// app/api/relay/[...path]/route.js
import { createRelayRouteHandler } from '@byok-relay/next';
export const { GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS } =
  createRelayRouteHandler({ relayUrl: process.env.RELAY_URL });
```

```jsx
// 'use client' component
import { useByokRelay, useStreamingChat } from '@byok-relay/next';
const { token, registerUser } = useByokRelay({ relayUrl: '/api/relay' });
const { messages, streamingContent, sendMessage } =
  useStreamingChat({ relayUrl: '/api/relay', token, model: 'openai/gpt-4o' });
```

npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@byok-relay/next

## Qwik City Integration (`@byok-relay/qwik`)

Qwik City server loaders, actions, and reactive stores for BYOK AI. `RELAY_URL` stays in `process.env` via Vite private env — never in the browser bundle.

```
npm install @byok-relay/qwik
```

- `createRelayLoader(opts)` — returns a Qwik City `routeLoader$`-compatible function; proxies GET requests to relay; reads `process.env.RELAY_URL`; `[...path]` maps to upstream sub-path; optional app_id allowlist
- `createRelayAction(opts)` — returns a `routeAction$`-compatible function for POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE; receives `{ path, token, body }` from Zod-validated form data
- `createByokRelayStore(opts)` — token registration + key CRUD + logout; pass `useStore()` result as `opts.store` for full Qwik reactivity; `init()` restores token from localStorage
- `createChatStore(opts)` — stateful non-streaming chat; openai/anthropic/groq/mistral/openrouter; systemPrompt + extraParams; optimistic rollback on error
- `createStreamingChatStore(opts)` — SSE streaming with AbortController; `stopStreaming()` partial-commits accumulated content; `streamingContent` updates in real-time
- `createRelayHealthStore(opts)` — polls `/health`; `startPolling(ms)` / `destroy()` for `useVisibleTask$` cleanup; `status` is `'ok' | 'degraded' | 'unknown'`
- `ByokRelayClient` — plain-JS class; works in `routeLoader$`, `routeAction$`, middleware, or browser; localStorage default; custom `storage` adapter for server-side / cookie session

```tsx
// src/routes/relay/[...path]/index.tsx — server-only proxy route
import { routeLoader$, routeAction$, zod$, z } from '@builder.io/qwik-city';
import { createRelayLoader, createRelayAction } from '@byok-relay/qwik';
export const useRelayData   = routeLoader$(createRelayLoader());
export const useRelayAction = routeAction$(createRelayAction(),
  zod$({ path: z.string(), token: z.string(), body: z.any().optional() }));
```

```tsx
// Client component — streaming chat
import { createByokRelayStore, createStreamingChatStore } from '@byok-relay/qwik';
const relayState  = useStore({ token: null, keys: [], loading: false, error: null });
const streamState = useStore({ messages: [], streamingContent: '', isStreaming: false, error: null });
const relay = createByokRelayStore({ store: relayState, relayUrl: '/relay' });
const chat  = createStreamingChatStore({ store: streamState, model: 'openai/gpt-4o-mini', relayUrl: '/relay' });
```

npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@byok-relay/qwik

## React Native / Expo Integration (`@byok-relay/expo`)

For React Native and Expo mobile apps. Uses AsyncStorage instead of localStorage for token persistence. Fetch-based SSE streaming requires a ReadableStream-capable implementation. Expo SDK 52+ provides `expo/fetch` and `ReadableStream` support automatically, so current Expo projects only need `@byok-relay/expo` plus AsyncStorage once the package is published. Install `expo-secure-store` only when using the optional SecureStore adapter. Older Expo SDKs or bare React Native apps must pass their own ReadableStream-capable `fetch` implementation or polyfill.

```bash
# After @byok-relay/expo is published:
npx expo install @react-native-async-storage/async-storage
npm install @byok-relay/expo

# Bare React Native:
npm install @byok-relay/expo @react-native-async-storage/async-storage

# Before publication, pack it from this source checkout and install the tarball in your app:
npm --workspace @byok-relay/expo pack
npm install /path/to/byok-relay/byok-relay-expo-1.0.0.tgz
```

```tsx
// Expo SDK 52+
import { fetch as expoFetch } from 'expo/fetch';
import { ByokRelayClient, useStreamingChat } from '@byok-relay/expo';

const client = new ByokRelayClient({ relayUrl: 'https://relay.byokrelay.com', fetch: expoFetch });

function ChatScreen() {
  const chat = useStreamingChat({ relayUrl: 'https://relay.byokrelay.com', model: 'openai/gpt-4o', fetch: expoFetch });
  return null;
}
```

Older Expo SDKs and bare React Native apps must pass a custom `fetch` implementation or polyfill with ReadableStream response bodies.

```tsx
import { useStreamingChat, useByokRelay } from '@byok-relay/expo';

function ApiKeySettings() {
  const { token, register, storeKey } = useByokRelay({ relayUrl: 'https://relay.byokrelay.com' });
  // register() obtains the relay token; storeKey() sends { key } with x-relay-token.
  return null;
}

function ChatScreen() {
  const { messages, streamingContent, sendMessage } = useStreamingChat({
    relayUrl: 'https://relay.byokrelay.com',
    model: 'openai/gpt-4o',
  });
  // render messages, streamingContent, and a send button
  return null;
}
```

With Expo SecureStore for platform secure storage of the relay-scoped token (`byok_relay_token:<encoded relay URL>`):
```tsx
import * as SecureStore from 'expo-secure-store';
import { ByokRelayClient } from '@byok-relay/expo';

const client = new ByokRelayClient({
  relayUrl: 'https://relay.byokrelay.com',
  storage: {
    getItem:    (k) => SecureStore.getItemAsync(k),
    setItem:    (k, v) => SecureStore.setItemAsync(k, v),
    removeItem: (k) => SecureStore.deleteItemAsync(k),
  },
});
```

Exported: `useByokRelay`, `useChat`, `useStreamingChat`, `useRelayHealth`, `ByokRelayClient`, `createAsyncStorage`.

npm: pending publication for @byok-relay/expo
